label: Mark van Roojen, Moral Cognitivism §3.4: cognitivist replies to Blackburn's comparison
locator: §3.4, 'Thus any reductive naturalist about moral properties will deny that premise of the argument' through 'analytic claims just are claims the linguistically competent must accept'
interpretation: Van Roojen's own comparison in the pinned SEP entry, not an attribution of these objections to the historical naturalists treated as primary sources here. He describes reductive naturalist opposition to the no-analytic-entailment premise, anti-Humean cognitivist opposition to an inert-belief/action-guidance division, and a cognitivist way to recognize analyticity in competence. These are serious live replies, not demonstrated defeats. The same §3.4 explicitly says it is not obvious nonreductive naturalist or nonnaturalist explanations must fail.
attribution: The passage states that naturalists may dispute the nonanalyticity premise, anti-Humean cognitivists may reject belief/motivation exclusivity, and cognitivists can accept analyticity as a competence requirement, which is the author's comparative objection rather than a conclusive success claim.
